moduleGuides.title: 1. Accessing the system
moduleGuides.purpose: Log in, complete OTP if enabled, change a forced password, and land on the workspace or dashboard that matches your role.
steps: Open the internal system URL in Chrome, Edge, or Firefox.
Sign in with the username or email and password issued by ICT.
Enter the OTP code if your account has OTP enabled.
Complete forced password change when prompted before continuing.
After Sign In, E-CIMES redirects you to your role landing page automatically.
Confirm the landing page and sidebar or ribbon match your assigned role, UI profile, and organisation scope.
tips: If login fails, confirm the account is active and approved.
Portal roles open a short Workspace sidebar; operators and ICT usually see the full ribbon.
Missing menus usually mean role permissions, UI profile, or organisation scope — not a system fault.
Never share passwords, OTP codes, or administrator accounts.

moduleGuides.title: 2. Home page, navigation, and workflow inbox
moduleGuides.audience: Operators, reviewers, ICT, and other non-portal staff (portal roles use their Workspace instead)
moduleGuides.purpose: Use the ribbon menu, Personal Dashboard, and pending workflow items when your role lands on the home page.
steps: If you land on Personal Dashboard (/), use the ribbon for Dashboard, Finance, Projects, Planning, Data, Procurement, Monitoring, Reports, Public, and Admin.
Portal role users (Village, Ward, Sub-County, Chief M&E, Sector M&E, engineers, Co-Finance, Contractor) primarily use the short Workspace sidebar — that is expected.
Open Dashboard > My Tasks (/my-tasks) to review escalations and approval steps assigned to you.
On the home page, review summary cards and any pending approvals or workflow tasks assigned to you.
Open a pending item from the inbox to approve, review, or complete the required action.
Use search and filters on list screens before concluding a record is missing.
Read success and error messages after saving, importing, or submitting records.
tips: Clear filters before reporting missing data.
The three-dot menu (top right) includes Help & Support.
For wide tables, browser zoom around 90%–110% improves readability.
My Tasks is your personal workflow inbox — check it regularly even if you primarily use a role workspace.

moduleGuides.title: 3. Role workspaces and landings
moduleGuides.audience: All portal roles and county leadership
moduleGuides.purpose: Dedicated landings for portal roles (Village, Ward, Sub-County, Chief M&E, Sector M&E, Resident/Chief Engineer, Co-Finance, Contractor) plus Summary Statistics for leadership. Village / Ward / Sub-County / Co-Finance workspaces also show Projects by department for scoped oversight.
steps: Village Administrator → Village M&E Workspace (/village-workspace): My drafts, monitoring visits, projects, documents.
Ward Administrator → Ward M&E Workspace (/ward-workspace): Ward review queue, village drafts, ward projects.
Sub-County Administrator → Sub-County M&E Workspace (/subcounty-workspace): Sub-county review queue and projects.
Department Chief Officer → Department Chief M&E Workspace (/chief-workspace): Chief approval queue; final approve for public.
Sector M&E Champion → Sector M&E Champions Workspace (/sector-me-workspace): read-only sector reports and pending chief items.
Resident Engineer → Resident Engineer Workspace (/resident-engineer-workspace): projects, photos, payments, certificate step 1.
Chief Engineer → Chief Engineer Workspace (/chief-engineer-workspace): certificate step 2 after Resident Engineer.
Co-Finance Officer → Co-Finance Workspace (/co-finance-workspace): certificate step 3, payments, county finance.
Contractor → Contractor Dashboard (/contractor-dashboard): payments, progress photos, project files for assigned projects.
Executive Supervisor / Executive Viewer / Project Lead → Summary Statistics (/summary-statistics) for briefing dashboards.
Other staff → Personal Dashboard (/) with the full ribbon menu.
On Village, Ward, Sub-County, and Co-Finance workspaces, use Projects by department to see which departments own which projects in your scope.
tips: Look at the sidebar group title after login to confirm which workspace you are in.
Organisation scope (ward, sub-county, department, sector) still limits which projects and reports you see.
ICT sets role, UI profile, and landing path under User Management.
Projects by department groups are case-insensitive (Kangundo and KANGUNDO roll up together).

moduleGuides.title: 4. AI Assistant and professional reports
moduleGuides.purpose: Ask questions about workflows, live project data, and generate downloadable Word/PDF reports from the current screen.
steps: Click the sparkle AI Assistant button at the bottom-right of any authenticated page.
Ask a question in chat — the assistant uses live data when available for your account scope.
For navigation questions (for example how to verify a certificate), it uses this Help & Support manual.
To create a formal document, click Generate Professional Report in the AI panel.
Choose report type, Word or PDF, and add instructions — the report uses data from the screen you are on.
Review AI output before official use; it is advisory and must be checked by responsible officers.
tips: Open the relevant dashboard or project screen first so the AI has the right context.
Finance dashboards produce finance-focused reports; monitoring screens produce monitoring-focused reports.
Super Admins can review AI usage under Admin > AI Usage.

moduleGuides.title: 5. Dashboards and executive views
moduleGuides.audience: Leadership, department heads, M&E, finance, and report users
moduleGuides.purpose: Review county performance through dedicated dashboards — each dashboard has a different focus.
steps: County leadership often lands directly on Summary Statistics after login.
Open Dashboard from the ribbon (when available) and choose the dashboard you need.
Project By Status — counts and charts by implementation status.
Project By Sector — sector/programme distribution.
Finance Dashboard — budget, paid, absorption, and finance KPIs.
Operations Dashboard — operational delivery and attention indicators.
Jobs & Impact — employment and beneficiary impact metrics.
Summary Statistics — county-wide summary cards and trends.
Regional Breakdown — subcounty/ward distribution.
Departmental Reports — department-level summaries.
GIS Dashboard and Project GIS Map — location-based views.
Personal Dashboard (home) — your scoped summary and workflow inbox.
Regional Breakdown Dashboard (/regional-reports) — balance and compare project distribution by sub-county and ward.
Project GIS Map (/project-gis-map) — locate projects on the map; investigate pins that look wrong or missing (incorrect GIS coordinates).
My Tasks (/my-tasks) — pending escalations and workflow approvals assigned to you.
Set filters (department, status, sector, ward, financial year) before interpreting figures.
Use drill-down links to open related project lists where available.
tips: Executives on the mobile app use Briefing mode rather than field checklist forms.
Dashboard totals depend on project visibility and data completeness.
Compare dashboard filters with Projects Registry filters if totals look inconsistent.
Use the AI Assistant on a dashboard to summarize that dashboard's data or generate a professional report.
Use Regional Breakdown and Project GIS Map together to spot uneven distribution and bad coordinates before planning new projects.

moduleGuides.title: 6. Projects Registry and implementation plans
moduleGuides.audience: Project officers, departments, M&E, finance, procurement, administrators
moduleGuides.purpose: Find, create, edit, and export projects; manage implementation plans.
steps: Open Projects > Projects Registry (/projects).
Search or filter by department, financial year, sector, status, subcounty, or ward.
Open a project row to open Project Details (/projects/:id) before editing.
Use Projects > Implementation Plans for cross-project implementation planning views.
Create a project only after confirming it does not already exist — or create from Budget Procurement Intake when converting a budget line.
Export after applying the required filters.
tips: Search before creating duplicates.
Project visibility affects dashboards, reports, certificates, GIS, and public publishing.
Registry filters should match Regional Breakdown filters when comparing distribution numbers.

moduleGuides.title: 7. Project details, evaluation, and evidence
moduleGuides.purpose: Maintain the single-project record: overview, milestones, status, documents, photos, teams, partners, funding, sites/GIS, BQ, certificates, and evaluations (baseline → achieved, result level).
steps: Open a project from Projects Registry (for example /projects/1) or from a workspace project list.
Review the overview and tabs before adding related records.
Update milestones and status using verified implementation evidence.
Check the map / sites tab — incorrect GIS coordinates show up on Project GIS Map county-wide.
Upload documents with clear names and correct categories.
Use the Certificates tab to create interim/final payment certificates (where authorised).
Use Project Evaluation Workbench (Projects menu) for structured evaluation workflows.
Link planning activities and risks so monitoring and reports stay consistent.

Open Projects → Project Evaluation to record evaluation lines: date, activity/indicator, baseline, target, achieved, performance %, reporting period (Baseline/Midline/Endline), and result level (output/outcome/impact).
Prefer indicators tagged as outcome or impact when measuring change for people — not only delivery outputs.
tips: Certificate PDFs include a QR code for public verification (top-right on page 1).
Evidence should support reported progress percentages.
Keep documents organised — audits and reports depend on them.
Fix GIS coordinates on the project before relying on map-based planning.
Use reporting period Baseline then Midline/Endline so programme scorecards can compare change over time.
Result level on the evaluation line is used in CIDP/ADP Programme Progress outcome columns.

moduleGuides.title: 8. Planning (CIDP, ADP, RRI, traceability)
moduleGuides.audience: Planning, M&E, department focal persons, administrators
moduleGuides.purpose: Maintain planning structures, ADP implementation, RRI programmes, budget traceability, KPI catalogues (with result levels), and CIDP/ADP programme progress scorecards (delivery + impact).
steps: Open Planning from the ribbon.
Maintain CIDP periods, ADP periods, sectors, programmes, and budget allocations.
Use ADP Implementation to track wishlist vs budgeted vs registered projects.
Open Planning > RRI Programmes (/planning/rri-programmes) for ward livelihood and multi-site RRI tracking (also under Monitoring).
Open an RRI programme detail page to manage sites and beneficiaries.
Use Budget Traceability to follow budget lines through implementation.
Maintain indicators, activities, risks, and reporting frequency catalogues.
Link catalogues to projects for consistent monitoring and reporting.
Open Planning → Indicators & KPIs (/planning/indicators) and set Result level: Output, Outcome, or Impact.

Open Planning → CIDP Programme Progress (/planning/cidp-programme-progress) for programme roll-ups of linkage, budget, avg progress, stalled projects, plus outcome achievement %, outcome lines, benefit realized, and community benefit.
Open Planning → ADP Programme Progress (/planning/adp-programme-progress) for the same impact scorecard on the annual plan.
tips: Catalogue changes affect reports — coordinate with M&E and ICT.
Search before creating new sectors, programmes, or risks.
Tag outcome/impact KPIs deliberately — programme scorecards weight those evaluation lines for outcome achievement %.
Export Excel/PDF from CIDP/ADP Programme Progress includes the impact columns.

moduleGuides.title: 9. Data import, beneficiaries, and upload logs
moduleGuides.audience: ICT admins, migration users, authorised data officers
moduleGuides.purpose: Import projects/budgets/beneficiaries safely and review upload logs.
steps: Open Data > Import Data and choose the correct import type.
Download and fill the official template without changing required column names.
Upload for preview and correct all validation errors before confirming.
Open Data Import Logs to verify completion.
Use Data > Beneficiary Registry to search and maintain beneficiary records.
On Beneficiary Registry, set Outcome status (enrolled → receiving benefit → benefit realized) and optional outcome notes so programme impact roll-ups can count realized benefits.
tips: Never import production data from an unverified spreadsheet.
Keep original and corrected files for audit reference.
Use benefit realized only when the intended benefit has actually reached the beneficiary — not merely upon enrollment.

moduleGuides.title: 10. Procurement and contractors
moduleGuides.purpose: Convert budget lines into registry projects, set project scope and planned BQ, enter contracted quotations, track procurement stages, and maintain the contractor registry.
steps: Open Procurement > Budget Procurement Intake (/procurement/budget-items).
Select an approved budget line and create / link the registry project (budget item → project).
Use Setup scope to define milestones and planned BQ (template, Excel, or manual) before quoting.
Use Quote to enter contracted quotation vs planned costs, then award when ready.
Open Procurement > Project Procurement for active procurement cases and stage tracking.
Review Procured Projects for completed history.
Maintain Contractor Registry and contractor types.
Link contractor user accounts in Contractor Management so the Contractor Dashboard works.
Contractors sign in to Contractor Dashboard for payments, photos, and files on assigned projects only.
tips: Always Setup scope before Quote — quotation entry needs a planned BQ baseline.
Stage updates must match approved procurement documentation.
Attach evidence to support audit review.
Unlinked contractor accounts show “Account not linked yet” on the portal.

moduleGuides.title: 11. Monitoring, PMC, and field data collection
moduleGuides.audience: M&E portal roles, M&E officers, project officers, ward teams, supervisors
moduleGuides.purpose: Record monitoring visits, run the Village→Ward→Sub-county→Chief approval chain, PMC ward reports, checklists, and mobile field collection.
steps: Portal M&E users should prefer their role workspace for day-to-day drafting, review, and approval.
Village: open Village M&E Workspace → My drafts → complete checklist and progress → submit to ward.
Ward: open Ward review queue → revise, return, or forward to sub-county.
Sub-County: review ward-forwarded reports → return with comments or forward to Department Chief.
Department Chief: open Chief approval queue → final approve (supports citizen dashboard publishing).
Sector M&E Champions use the read-only sector workspace for oversight across mapped departments.
Open Monitoring > Project Monitoring for structured project monitoring records (ribbon users).
Use PMC Ward Reports, Ward Accountability, and Monitoring > Checklists & visits as required.
Download CIMES Mobile from Dashboard or workspace mobile quick action.
Field staff sign in on the app, sync checklists, select a project, and submit visits offline when needed.
Village Field Monitoring checklist loads work stages / milestones from the project record (not a fixed pick-list). Sync the mobile app after template updates.
In the Community & beneficiary feedback section, answer Community benefit realized and Access improved (Yes/No) plus optional impact notes — these feed programme community-benefit scorecards.
tips: Approval chain: Village draft → Ward → Sub-county → Chief → public.
Monitoring records should be timely and linked to the correct project.
Mobile app sync requires network — pull down to refresh checklists after login.
Escalate persistent delays, low absorption, or unresolved complaints.
If the web checklist still shows old fixed work stages, discard the template draft on Data Collection Tools and reload from the server.
On CIMES Mobile, pull to Sync on Checklists after ICT updates the village template.

moduleGuides.title: 12. Finance, payment certificates, and verification
moduleGuides.audience: Finance users, Resident/Chief Engineers, Co-Finance, accounts, project officers, leadership, public verifiers
moduleGuides.purpose: Review finance performance, create payment certificates, complete the engineer/Co-Finance approval chain, and verify certificate authenticity.
steps: Open Finance Dashboard for high-level financial KPIs (or Co-Finance Workspace for portal finance tools).
Use Payment List for payment records and filters.
Use Payment Certificates (Finance menu) for county-wide certificate records.
On a project, open the Certificates tab to create interim/final certificates and generate PDFs.
Approval order for payment certificates: Resident Engineer Workspace (step 1) → Chief Engineer Workspace (step 2) → Co-Finance Workspace (step 3).
Generated certificate PDFs include a QR code labelled Scan to verify this certificate.
To verify any certificate: Finance > Verify Certificate (or open /verify-certificate).
Enter the certificate number manually OR scan the QR code on the printed PDF with a phone camera.
The verification page shows whether the certificate is valid and displays project and contractor details.
Use Funding Sources Report, Project Finance Overview, and Pending Bills for deeper analysis.
tips: Do not skip approval steps — certificates move only after the previous role approves.
Verify certificates before relying on printed or shared copies.
Verification works without logging in — citizens and contractors can use the public page.
Logged-in staff see a link to open the related project from verification results.

moduleGuides.title: 13. Reports, report library, and scheduling
moduleGuides.purpose: Find built-in reports, export official outputs, and schedule recurring reports.
steps: Open Reports > Reports hub — searchable index of all report screens.
Choose the report (APR, County Operations, Status, Absorption, Pending Bills, Yearly Trends, PMC, etc.).
Set filters (department, financial year, status, ward, dates).
Review totals and exceptions before exporting.
Save approved outputs to Report Library where applicable.
Use Scheduled Reports for recurring email distribution.
Built-in reports are separate from AI Professional Reports — use Reports hub for standard county templates.
tips: Record filter criteria when sharing exported reports.
Reports are only as accurate as underlying project, finance, and monitoring data.

moduleGuides.title: 14. Public dashboard and citizen engagement
moduleGuides.purpose: Manage what citizens see and how they engage.
steps: Review the public dashboard URL and approved public projects.
Use Public Approval to approve projects for citizen visibility.
Department Chief M&E final approval of monitoring reports also supports publishing toward the citizen dashboard.
Moderate feedback and manage announcements.
Only approved content should appear on public pages.
tips: Avoid publishing sensitive internal notes.
Coordinate sensitive responses with the responsible department.

moduleGuides.title: 15. User administration and mobile app releases
moduleGuides.purpose: Manage users, roles, organisation scope, UI profiles, landing paths, OTP, mobile app releases, and AI usage.
steps: Open Admin > User Management for accounts, roles, organisation scope, and UI profiles.
Assign the correct landing path for portal roles (for example /ward-workspace or /resident-engineer-workspace).
Link contractor users to contractor records when enabling Contractor Dashboard access.
Use Admin > Mobile App Usage to review CIMES Mobile adoption.
Use Admin > AI Usage (Super Admin) for assistant cost and activity.
Staff download CIMES Mobile from Dashboard > CIMES Mobile (Android) or /mobile-app when signed in.
tips: Use least privilege for roles, UI profiles, and scope.
Document administrator actions for audit.
Portal role names take precedence over a mismatched UI profile landing path.

moduleGuides.title: 16. Metadata, workflows, and audit trail
moduleGuides.purpose: Maintain master data, approval levels, workflows, and investigate audit logs.
steps: Open Admin > Metadata Management or relevant setup pages.
Search before adding duplicate metadata values.
Use Audit Trail to investigate user actions and support incidents.
Test workflow changes before rolling out to users.
tips: Duplicate metadata causes reporting errors.
Use audit trail facts when investigating incidents.

moduleGuides.title: 17. Measuring project and programme impact
moduleGuides.audience: M&E, planning, department focal persons, leadership, administrators
moduleGuides.purpose: Go beyond delivery progress (% complete) to evaluate whether programmes and projects change outcomes for people. Combine indicator result levels, project evaluation lines (baseline→endline), beneficiary outcome status, and structured community visit answers into CIDP/ADP programme scorecards.
steps: Distinguish layers: Progress = how far implementation has gone; Impact = whether intended benefits and outcomes are realized.
Planning → Indicators & KPIs: create/edit KPIs and set Result level to Output (delivery), Outcome (change for people), or Impact (longer-term effect).
Link activities/indicators to projects (Projects → Activity links) with baseline and target values.

Projects → Project Evaluation: for each line, set Evaluation date, pick activity/indicator, record Baseline, Target, Achieved, optional Performance %, Reporting period (Baseline / Midline / Endline / quarterly), Result level, and Remarks.
Capture Midline and Endline evaluations against the same indicators used at Baseline so change is comparable.
Data → Beneficiary Registry: update Outcome status as people move from enrolled to receiving benefit to benefit realized (add outcome notes when useful).
Village Field Monitoring (web or CIMES Mobile): complete Community benefit realized and Access improved, plus impact notes from community comments.

Planning → CIDP Programme Progress: review delivery columns (projects, linkage, avg progress, stalled, budgets) and impact columns (Outcome ach. %, Outcome lines, Benefit realized, Community benefit).
Planning → ADP Programme Progress: select the ADP plan and review the same delivery + impact scorecard for the financial year.
Export Excel or PDF from the programme progress pages for M&E and leadership packs.
Jobs & Impact Dashboard remains useful for jobs/beneficiary volume; use Programme Progress for outcome achievement against CIDP/ADP structures.
tips: Do not treat % complete alone as impact — a finished project can still have weak community benefit.
Prefer outcome/impact result levels on evaluation lines that measure change for people.
Village checklist answers only count when the coded Yes/No fields are used (not free text alone).
If impact columns show dashes, check that projects are linked to the CIDP/ADP programme and that evaluations/beneficiary outcomes/visits exist.
Hard-refresh the browser after releases; mobile users should Sync checklists after template updates.

quickTasks: Find my role workspace after login
Confirm the sidebar title (Village M&E, Ward M&E, Resident Engineer, Co-Finance, Contractor, etc.) or Summary Statistics / Personal Dashboard.
Complete checklist and progress, attach evidence, submit to ward.
Review a report at ward / sub-county / chief
Open the review or approval queue; revise, return with comments, forward, or finally approve.
Projects > Projects Registry (or My projects in workspace)
Search by name/code or filter by department, status, ward, or financial year.
Projects > Project Status or Project Details
Open the project, add status/progress, attach evidence.
Complete BQ where required, create interim/final certificate, generate PDF with QR code.
Approve in order: Resident Engineer (step 1), Chief Engineer (step 2), Co-Finance (step 3).
Enter certificate number OR scan QR on the PDF. Public URL: /verify-certificate?cert=NUMBER
Use Request payment, Upload progress photos, or Submit project files for assigned projects.
Search for the report, set filters, review totals, export.
Open the relevant workspace or dashboard first, then Generate Professional Report → choose type, Word/PDF.
Monitoring > Project Monitoring or role workspace
Find project, add visit/checklist notes, save observations.
Filter ward/period, complete ward PMC entries.
Create/edit templates; record visit submissions on web or mobile.
Download APK while signed in; install on Android; sign in and sync checklists. Executives use Briefing mode.
Download template, preview, fix errors, confirm import.
Public > Public Approval (and Chief M&E final approval)
Review content before citizen visibility; Chief M&E approval feeds public publishing.
Open /regional-reports, filter by financial year, compare sub-county and ward counts before proposing new sites.
Open /project-gis-map, filter regionally, inspect pins that are missing, clustered wrongly, or outside the expected ward.
Open /projects, search/filter, then open a project for details.
Open /projects/:id (for example /projects/1); review tabs, evidence, sites/GIS, and certificates.
Open /procurement/budget-items, create/link the registry project from the budget line.
Open Setup project scope & costs; define milestones and planned BQ before quotation.
Open Contracted quotation vs planned; enter quoted costs, optionally award.
Open /planning/rri-programmes; create or open a programme for multi-site / beneficiary tracking.
Open /my-tasks for escalations and workflow approvals assigned to you.
Planning → CIDP or ADP Programme Progress (+ Project Evaluation)

Tag KPIs as outcome/impact; record Baseline→Endline evaluations; update beneficiary outcome status; complete village community benefit fields; read Outcome ach. % and Benefit realized on programme progress.
Select project; add line with date, activity/indicator, baseline, target, achieved, reporting period, and result level (output/outcome/impact).
Open /planning/indicators; create or edit a KPI; choose Result level Output, Outcome, or Impact.
Open /planning/cidp-programme-progress; check linkage, progress, stalled, and impact columns; export Excel/PDF if needed.
Open /planning/adp-programme-progress; select ADP plan; review delivery and outcome scorecards.
Edit a beneficiary; set Outcome status (e.g. benefit realized) and optional outcome notes.
See projects by department in a workspace
Open the workspace landing; use Projects by department to see ownership within your scope.
troubleshootingRows: Cannot log in
Wrong password, inactive account, pending approval, OTP issue.
Confirm username, account status, password reset. Escalate OTP failures to ICT.
Wrong home page after login
Role or UI profile landing path differs from expectation.
Note the sidebar/workspace title and your role name; ask ICT to check role, UI profile, and landing path.
Missing menu item / short sidebar only
Portal role uses a dedicated workspace instead of the full ribbon.
Use the Workspace sidebar for your role. Full ribbon is for operators/admins — not a fault.
Cannot see expected project
Active filters or scope excludes the project.
Clear filters, verify department, ward, sub-county, sector, and user scope.
Dashboard figures look wrong
Filters differ or source data incomplete.
Record filters, compare with Projects Registry.
M&E report stuck in queue
Waiting at next approval step or returned with comments.
Check Village drafts / Ward review / Sub-county review / Chief approval tabs and comments.
Certificate waiting forever
Previous approval step not completed.
Confirm Resident Engineer → Chief Engineer → Co-Finance order; check the correct workspace Certificates screen.
Contractor: Account not linked yet
User not linked in Contractor Management / registry.
Ask Procurement or ICT to link the contractor account and assign projects.
AI gives generic answers
Question is about navigation, or screen has no live data context.
Open the relevant page first; for how-to questions see Help & Support. Ask again on the correct dashboard.
AI reports look the same on different dashboards
Report generated without opening the target screen first.
Navigate to the specific dashboard or workspace, then use Generate Professional Report.
Certificate not verified
Wrong number, voided certificate, or typo.
Re-enter number exactly as on PDF; try scanning QR code instead.
QR scan does not open verify page
Camera app blocked or wrong QR.
Manually open Finance > Verify Certificate and type the certificate number from the PDF header.
Mobile app shows offline mode
Network issue or sync failed after login.
Check connectivity, pull down to sync on Checklists tab, or reinstall latest APK from /mobile-app.
Import failed
Template errors or invalid metadata.
Review preview errors, correct spreadsheet, upload again.
Authorization error
Signed in but missing privilege.
Capture module/action; ask administrator to review permissions and UI profile.
Impact / Outcome columns are empty on Programme Progress
No linked projects, or no evaluation/beneficiary/visit impact data yet.
Link projects to CIDP/ADP programmes; add evaluation lines with outcome/impact levels; set beneficiary outcome status; complete village community Yes/No fields.
Village checklist still shows old fixed work stages
Stale browser template draft or mobile checklist cache.
On Data Collection Tools, discard draft and reload; on mobile, Sync Checklists. Milestones come from the project record.
Cannot find CIDP / ADP Programme Progress
Missing planning privilege or outdated bookmark.
Confirm strategic_plan / project read privileges; open Planning → CIDP Programme Progress or ADP Programme Progress.
roleGuidance: County leadership (Executive Supervisor / Viewer)
Land on Summary Statistics. Use Dashboard ribbon, Reports hub, AI summaries, and mobile Briefing mode for status and finance oversight.
CECM / County Viewer / view-only Chief Officers
Scoped dashboards and department oversight via the ribbon; read-only according to privileges and organisation scope.
Village Administrator
Village M&E Workspace (/village-workspace): draft monitoring reports, attach evidence, submit to ward.
Ward Administrator
Ward M&E Workspace (/ward-workspace): review/revise village reports, forward to sub-county; PMC ward reports.
Sub-County Administrator
Sub-County M&E Workspace (/subcounty-workspace): return or forward ward-approved reports to Department Chief.
Department Chief Officer (M&E)
Department Chief M&E Workspace (/chief-workspace): final approve monitoring reports for citizen visibility.
Sector M&E Champion
Sector M&E Champions Workspace (/sector-me-workspace): read-only sector portfolio and pending chief items.
Resident Engineer
Resident Engineer Workspace: projects, progress photos, payment requests, first-step certificate approval.
Chief Engineer
Chief Engineer Workspace: second-step certificate approval after Resident Engineer.
Co-Finance Officer
Co-Finance Workspace: final certificate approval, payment requests, and county finance tools.
Contractor
Contractor Dashboard: request payments, upload progress photos and project files for assigned projects only.
Department / County operators & reviewers
Personal Dashboard with full ribbon — projects, progress, evidence, and review queues.
Planning users
Maintain CIDP/ADP, RRI, budget traceability, catalogues, and programme alignment.
M&E / Finance / Procurement staff (ribbon)
Use Monitoring, Finance, or Procurement ribbon modules matching their function.
Field collectors
CIMES Mobile: sync checklists, record visits offline, upload when connected.
Public engagement users
Public Approval, feedback moderation, announcements.
ICT administrators
Users, roles, UI profiles, landing paths, metadata, audit, mobile releases, AI usage monitoring.
goodPracticeItems: After login, confirm you are on the expected role workspace (sidebar title) or Summary Statistics / Personal Dashboard.
Search before creating duplicate projects, users, or metadata values.
Check active filters and organisation scope before reporting missing data.
Follow the M&E chain: Village draft → Ward → Sub-county → Chief approve → public.
Follow certificate approvals in order: Resident Engineer → Chief Engineer → Co-Finance.
Verify payment certificates using Finance > Verify Certificate or the QR code on the PDF.
Open the correct workspace or dashboard before generating AI professional reports.
Review AI output before official submission.
Use clear comments when returning or forwarding monitoring reports and certificates.
Attach evidence where the process requires proof.
Link contractor accounts in Contractor Management before expecting Contractor Dashboard access.
Use least privilege for roles, UI profiles, and organisation scope.
Do not share passwords, OTPs, or confidential citizen data in screenshots.
Use Regional Breakdown and Project GIS Map when balancing new projects across wards and sub-counties.
Correct GIS coordinates on project details when map pins look wrong.
On Budget Procurement Intake, Setup scope before entering a quotation.
Measure impact with Baseline → Midline/Endline evaluations on outcome/impact indicators — not only % complete.
Update beneficiary Outcome status when benefits are realized so programme scorecards stay accurate.
Use Village Field Monitoring community Yes/No impact fields so community feedback rolls up to CIDP/ADP progress.
supportChecklist: Your name, department, role, and contact.
Workspace or landing page you see after login (and sidebar title if shown).
Exact module or page (route URL if possible).
Project name/code, certificate number, report name, or user account involved.
Action attempted and exact error message.
Screenshot with passwords and personal data hidden.
Date/time and whether issue affects one user or many.

aiAssistantGuide.title: AI Assistant and professional reports
aiAssistantGuide.summary: The sparkle AI button (bottom-right) answers questions using live data for your account and this Help manual for navigation. Professional reports are generated from the screen you are currently viewing.
steps: Navigate to the workspace, dashboard, project, or report screen that matches your question.
Open AI Assistant and ask a question or click Generate Professional Report.
Choose report type and Word/PDF — finance dashboards favour Finance Summary; monitoring screens favour Monitoring Summary.
Review the download before official use.
tips: For how-to questions (verify certificate, find a menu), the assistant should cite exact menu paths from Help & Support.
Super Admins monitor usage at Admin > AI Usage.
Portal users can open the AI Assistant from their workspace so summaries use the correct scoped context.

dashboardGuides.title: Finance Dashboard
dashboardGuides.purpose: Budget allocation, disbursement, absorption, and finance KPIs for accessible projects.

navigationTopics.title: Find your role workspace after login
navigationTopics.summary: E-CIMES opens the home screen that matches your role: a dedicated Workspace, Summary Statistics, or Personal Dashboard.
steps: Sign in with your county credentials (and OTP if enabled).
Wait for the automatic redirect — do not hunt for a different home unless ICT instructed you to.
Read the sidebar title: Village M&E, Ward M&E, Sub-County M&E, Department Chief M&E, Sector M&E Champions, Resident Engineer, Chief Engineer, Co-Finance, or Contractor.
Leadership roles open Summary Statistics; operators and ICT open Personal Dashboard with the full ribbon.
Use Help & Support (three-dot menu) if the landing does not match your job function.
tips: A short sidebar is normal for portal roles.
Ask ICT to review role, UI profile, and landing path if the wrong workspace opens.

navigationTopics.title: Village → Ward → Sub-County → Chief M&E approval
navigationTopics.menuPath: Village / Ward / Sub-County / Chief M&E Workspace
navigationTopics.summary: Monitoring reports move through Village draft, Ward review, Sub-County review, and Department Chief final approval before public visibility.
steps: Village Administrator: open Village M&E Workspace → My drafts → complete checklist and progress status → submit to ward.
Ward Administrator: open Ward review queue → revise or return with comments → forward to sub-county.
Sub-County Administrator: open Sub-county review queue → return or forward to Department Chief.
Department Chief Officer: open Chief approval queue → final approve.
Sector M&E Champions may oversee All sector reports and Pending chief approval (read-only).
Approved outcomes support publishing toward the citizen dashboard according to county procedure.
tips: Always read return comments before resubmitting.
Attach photos and documents that support reported progress.
Use Monitoring → Village monitoring workflow when available on the ribbon for the same chain.

navigationTopics.title: Payment certificate approval (Resident → Chief → Co-Finance)
navigationTopics.menuPath: Resident Engineer / Chief Engineer / Co-Finance Workspace → Certificates
navigationTopics.summary: Payment certificates are approved in three workspace steps: Resident Engineer, then Chief Engineer, then Co-Finance Officer.
steps: Create or receive the certificate on the project Certificates tab (authorised staff).
Resident Engineer: open Resident Engineer Workspace → Certificates and complete first approval.
Chief Engineer: open Chief Engineer Workspace → Payment Certificates for second approval.
Co-Finance Officer: open Co-Finance Workspace → Payment Certificates for final approval.
Generate or download the PDF and verify with Finance → Verify Certificate (QR or certificate number).
tips: Certificates appear at each step only after the previous role approves.
Contractors track related payment requests from Contractor Dashboard.

navigationTopics.title: Contractor Dashboard
navigationTopics.summary: Contractors use a dedicated portal for assigned projects: payment requests, progress photos, and project files.
steps: Sign in with a Contractor role account that is linked in Contractor Management.
Land on Contractor Dashboard (/contractor-dashboard).
Use Request payment for payment requests on assigned projects.
Upload progress photos and submit project files from the Contractor sidebar.
Track payment status from the payments area of the portal.
tips: If you see “Account not linked yet”, contact Procurement or ICT.
Only assigned projects are visible.

navigationTopics.title: Verify a payment certificate
navigationTopics.summary: Confirm whether a Machakos County payment certificate is genuine. Works for staff and the public without login.
steps: Open Finance → Verify Certificate in the ribbon (or go to /verify-certificate).
Option A — Scan: use your phone camera on the QR code printed on the certificate PDF (labelled Scan to verify this certificate).
Option B — Manual: type the certificate number exactly as shown on the PDF header.
Press Verify and read the result — valid certificates show project name, contractor, dates, and status.
Staff users can click through to open the related project record.
tips: QR links open /verify-certificate?cert=CERTIFICATE_NUMBER automatically.
If verification fails, check for typos or confirm the certificate was generated in this system.

navigationTopics.title: Create and manage payment certificates
navigationTopics.menuPath: Finance → Payment Certificates; or Project Details → Certificates tab
navigationTopics.summary: Staff create interim/final certificates per project; engineers and Co-Finance approve in sequence; PDFs include signatures and a verification QR code.
steps: Open the project in Projects Registry → Certificates tab (or Finance → Payment Certificates for the county list).
Complete bill of quantities requirements where configured.
Create interim or final certificate with correct amounts and references.
Approve in order: Resident Engineer Workspace → Chief Engineer Workspace → Co-Finance Workspace.
Generate PDF — the QR code on the PDF links to the public verify page.
tips: Always verify issued PDFs using Finance → Verify Certificate before external sharing.
If a certificate does not appear for approval, confirm the previous step was completed.

navigationTopics.title: Generate a professional AI report
navigationTopics.menuPath: AI Assistant button (bottom-right on any page)
navigationTopics.summary: Downloadable Word/PDF reports built from live data on the screen you are viewing.
steps: Navigate to the dashboard or report screen that matches your topic (finance dashboard for finance, monitoring for monitoring, etc.).
Click the sparkle AI Assistant button at the bottom-right.
Click Generate Professional Report OR ask in chat for a well formatted report.
Select report type (Project Status, Finance Summary, CIDP Linkage, Monitoring Summary, General M&E).
Choose Word (.docx) or PDF and add specific instructions.
Download and review before official submission.
tips: Reports differ by screen — open Finance Dashboard before a finance report, Status Report before a status report, etc.
Chat summaries and professional reports use different outputs — use Generate Professional Report for downloadable documents.

navigationTopics.title: CIMES Mobile (Android)
navigationTopics.summary: Android app for offline checklist data collection and executive briefing.
steps: Sign in to the web system and open Dashboard → CIMES Mobile (Android) or /mobile-app.
Download and install the published APK.
Open CIMES Mobile, sign in with county credentials.
On Checklists tab, pull down to sync templates and projects.
Tap a checklist, select project, complete form, submit (queues offline if needed).
tips: Install the latest published version when prompted.
Pull down on Checklists to retry sync if offline mode appears.
Executive Supervisor / Viewer style roles use Briefing mode on mobile, not field checklist forms.
Village workspace also offers a mobile app quick action.

navigationTopics.title: Checklists and monitoring visits
navigationTopics.summary: Web tool to build checklist templates and record visit submissions; syncs with the mobile collector.
steps: Open Monitoring → Checklists & visits.
Create or edit checklist templates with sections and questions.
Record visit submissions linked to projects.
Export visit PDFs where available.
Field teams can use the mobile app for offline collection.
tips: Template changes apply to new visits — coordinate updates with field teams.

navigationTopics.title: Find the right built-in report
navigationTopics.summary: Searchable index of all standard county reports (separate from AI professional reports).
steps: Open Reports → Reports hub.
Search by report name or keyword.
Open the report card, set filters, generate/export.
Use Report Library to archive approved outputs.
Use Scheduled Reports for recurring email delivery.
tips: Built-in reports use county templates; AI professional reports use the sparkle assistant.

navigationTopics.title: PMC ward reports
navigationTopics.summary: Ward-level Project Monitoring Committee reporting.
steps: Open Monitoring → PMC Ward Reports.
Filter by ward, period, or financial year as required.
Complete or review ward PMC entries.
Export or submit according to county procedure.

navigationTopics.title: Finance Dashboard
navigationTopics.summary: High-level finance KPIs for projects in your scope.
steps: Open Dashboard → Finance Dashboard.
Set department, financial year, and status filters.
Review summary cards and charts.
Use AI Assistant here for finance summaries or Finance Summary professional reports.

navigationTopics.title: Balance projects with Regional Breakdown
navigationTopics.summary: Compare project and budget distribution across sub-counties and wards to support balanced allocation.
steps: Open Dashboard → Regional Breakdown Dashboard (/regional-reports).
Set financial year and other filters.
Compare counts and budgets by sub-county and ward.
Cross-check uneven areas on Project GIS Map and in Projects Registry before proposing new projects.
tips: Use the same filters on Projects Registry when totals look inconsistent.

navigationTopics.title: Project GIS Map and coordinate quality
navigationTopics.summary: View project locations on the county map and spot missing or incorrect GIS coordinates.
steps: Open Dashboard → Project GIS Map (/project-gis-map).
Filter by sub-county, ward, department, or status as needed.
Inspect pins that are missing, outside the expected ward, or clustered incorrectly.
Open the project details record and correct sites / coordinates, then refresh the map.
tips: Incorrect coordinates affect public maps and regional planning decisions.

navigationTopics.title: Use the Projects Registry
navigationTopics.summary: Search, filter, create, and open county projects from the central registry.
steps: Open Projects → Projects Registry (/projects).
Search by name/code or filter by department, status, ward, sector, or financial year.
Open a row to view Project Details.
Create a project only after confirming it does not already exist.
tips: Budget-linked projects may originate from Budget Procurement Intake instead of a blank create form.

navigationTopics.title: Open project details
navigationTopics.summary: Single-project hub for overview, evidence, sites/GIS, BQ, certificates, teams, and status.
steps: From Projects Registry, open a project (URL form /projects/:id, for example /projects/1).
Review overview tabs before editing.
Update progress, documents, photos, and sites/GIS as required.
Use Certificates when authorised; verify PDFs after generation.
tips: Some tabs may be hidden by your UI profile.

navigationTopics.title: Budget item → project, scope, and quotation
navigationTopics.summary: Convert an approved budget line into a registry project, set scope/planned BQ, then enter the contracted quotation.
steps: Open Procurement → Budget Procurement Intake (/procurement/budget-items).
Create or link the registry project from the budget line.
Click Setup scope — define milestones and planned BQ (template, Excel, or manual).
Click Quote — enter contracted quotation vs planned costs; award when ready.
Continue procurement stages and contractor assignment as required.
tips: Setup scope before Quote — quotation needs a planned BQ baseline.
Scope setup is also available from engineer / Co-Finance workspace project lists.

navigationTopics.title: RRI Programmes
navigationTopics.menuPath: Planning → RRI Programmes (also Monitoring → RRI Programmes)
navigationTopics.summary: Manage Rapid Results / ward livelihood programmes with multi-site and beneficiary tracking.
steps: Open Planning → RRI Programmes or Monitoring → RRI Programmes (/planning/rri-programmes).
Create or open a programme.
Maintain sites and beneficiaries on the programme detail page.
Link related projects so monitoring and reports stay aligned.

navigationTopics.title: My Tasks workflow inbox
navigationTopics.summary: Personal list of escalations and workflow approval steps assigned to you.
steps: Open Dashboard → My Tasks (/my-tasks).
Review pending escalations and approval steps.
Open an item to complete, approve, or return according to county procedure.
Return to My Tasks after acting to confirm the queue updated.
tips: Portal workspace queues (Ward review, Chief approval, certificate steps) complement My Tasks — check both when relevant.

navigationTopics.title: Measure project and programme impact
navigationTopics.menuPath: Planning → CIDP / ADP Programme Progress; Projects → Project Evaluation
navigationTopics.summary: Track delivery progress and evaluate outcomes/impact using indicators, project evaluations, beneficiary outcome status, village community fields, and CIDP/ADP programme scorecards.
steps: Set Result level on Planning → Indicators & KPIs (output / outcome / impact).
Record Project Evaluation lines with reporting period Baseline, Midline, or Endline.
Update Beneficiary Registry Outcome status when benefits are realized.
Complete Village Field Monitoring community benefit and access-improved questions.
Open Planning → CIDP Programme Progress or ADP Programme Progress to review Outcome ach. %, Benefit realized, and Community benefit alongside delivery metrics.
tips: % complete is progress; Outcome ach. % and Benefit realized measure impact.
Link projects to programmes or scorecards will stay empty.

navigationTopics.title: CIDP Programme Progress
navigationTopics.summary: Programme roll-up of linked project budgets, progress, stalled projects, and impact scorecards.
steps: Open Planning → CIDP Programme Progress (/planning/cidp-programme-progress).
Review projects, linkage %, avg progress, stalled, and budgets.
Read impact columns: Outcome ach. %, Outcome lines, Benefit realized, Community benefit.
Export Excel or PDF for leadership packs.

navigationTopics.title: ADP Programme Progress
navigationTopics.summary: Annual Development Plan programme roll-up with delivery and impact scorecards.
steps: Open Planning → ADP Programme Progress (/planning/adp-programme-progress).
Select the ADP plan / financial year.
Review ADP rows, registry links, budgets, progress, and impact columns.

navigationTopics.title: Project Evaluation Workbench
navigationTopics.summary: Structured evaluation lines per project for baseline/target/achieved performance by result level and reporting period.
steps: Open Projects → Project Evaluation.
Select a project and add or edit an evaluation line.
Set reporting period and result level; save baseline, target, and achieved values.
tips: Selecting a linked activity prefills baseline and target from Activity links.

navigationTopics.title: Indicators & KPIs (result levels)
navigationTopics.summary: Catalogue of KPIs with measurement types and result levels used in evaluations and programme scorecards.
steps: Open Planning → Indicators & KPIs (/planning/indicators).
Create or edit a KPI; set measurement type and Result level.
